prompt.context: You have been asked to estimate the size of the acoustic piano market in the state of New Hampshire for the year 2012.
prompt.question: What is the 2012 market size of acoustic pianos in the state of New Hampshire?

clarifying_info.q: What counts as an acoustic piano?
clarifying_info.a: Acoustic piano includes upright, grand, and baby grand pianos. Digital keyboards are out of scope.

clarifying_info.q: Should I include commercial venues like concert halls or retail inventory?
clarifying_info.a: It is safe to focus on the residential market only — ignore concert halls, retail store inventory, etc.

clarifying_info.q: What is the population of New Hampshire?
clarifying_info.a: The US has a population of about 300 million spread across 50 states, so the average is 6 million per state. NH is one of the smaller states.

clarifying_info.q: What is the average household size?
clarifying_info.a: A reasonable estimate is the US average of about 2.5 people per household, or 2–3 if rounding.

clarifying_info.q: What is the average price of an acoustic piano?
clarifying_info.a: Prices vary by type (upright vs. grand). A reasonable estimate is $5,000–$10,000.

framework: Define the residential market scope (exclude concert halls, retail inventory)
Break market size into key drivers: Population → Households → Piano-owning households → Total piano value → Annual market (via replacement rate)
Equation: Market Size = (NH Population / Avg Household Size) × % HH Owning Piano × Avg Piano Price × Replacement Rate
Estimate each variable with reasoned assumptions, using US benchmarks as anchors
Sanity-check the final number and discuss sensitivity to key assumptions

questions.prompt: Walk through your approach before calculating. What equation will you use?
questions.guidance: Candidate should articulate the full driver tree before touching numbers: Population → HH count → piano-owning HH → total stock value → annual purchases via replacement rate. Equation: (NH Population / HH Size) × % owning piano × avg price × (1 / piano lifespan).

questions.prompt: Estimate the population of New Hampshire.
questions.guidance: US population ~300M, 50 states → average 6M per state. NH is one of the smallest states; a reasonable estimate is 1–2M. Using 1.5M is well-supported.

math.setup: US population / number of states = average; NH is below average
steps: NH is among the smallest states → estimate 1–1.5M; use 1.5M

questions.prompt: Estimate the number of households in New Hampshire.
questions.guidance: Divide NH population by average household size (~2.5, the US average). Rounding to 2–3 is acceptable.

math.setup: HH count = Population / Avg HH size

questions.prompt: What share of households own an acoustic piano, and why?
questions.guidance: Candidate should reason through factors: NH has relatively higher household wealth than most US states (supporting higher ownership); acoustic pianos compete with electric keyboards (suppressing share); pianos are large and expensive (suppressing share); macroeconomic/elastic demand. US baseline is likely under 5% of all households. Acceptable range: 3–10%, with 5% being a well-reasoned midpoint.

questions.prompt: Estimate the average price of an acoustic piano.
questions.guidance: Upright pianos are cheaper than grand pianos. A blended average of $5,000–$10,000 is reasonable. Using $7,500 as a midpoint is well-supported.

questions.prompt: How do you convert the stock of pianos into an annual market size? What is the replacement rate?
questions.guidance: Candidate must recognise that households do not buy a new piano every year; annual market = total stock value ÷ average piano lifespan (or × replacement rate). Pianos are very durable instruments; lifespan of 30–50 years is reasonable. Using 40 years (replacement rate = 1/40 = 2.5%) is well-supported.

math.setup: Annual market = (Piano-owning HH × Avg price) / Piano lifespan

questions.prompt: What is the final annual market size for acoustic pianos in New Hampshire?
questions.guidance: Strong candidates arrive confidently at ~$5–6M/year, state the key assumptions driving the estimate, and offer a brief sensitivity discussion (e.g., if ownership is 10% instead of 5%, market doubles to ~$11M).

math.setup: Full equation: (Population / HH size) × % owning × avg price / lifespan

recommendation: The 2012 residential acoustic piano market in New Hampshire is approximately $5.6 million per year, based on ~1.5M residents, ~600K households, ~5% piano ownership, an average piano price of $7,500, and a 40-year replacement cycle.
risks: Ownership rate is the most sensitive assumption — doubling it to 10% doubles the market to ~$11M
Piano lifespan assumption (30–50 years) meaningfully swings the annual figure
NH's higher-than-average household wealth could push ownership above the US baseline
Shift toward digital keyboards could reduce acoustic piano ownership over time
next_steps: Validate ownership rate with consumer survey data or industry reports
Refine average price estimate by weighting upright vs. grand piano mix
Consider whether commercial demand (schools, churches) is material enough to add a separate segment
